_comment: The route limit covers the pre-join entrance (#712); SpaceCall loads the admitted call after Join (#730), and builds its join client from the generated ChalkPublicApi (only the unauthenticated /v1/public operations), so the MCP OAuth contract (#814) stays out of the route. The route measures about 205.5 KiB and its ceiling is 217 KiB, down from 219. Five fresh-context bundle-only runs per revision on Linux x64, 8-core Intel Xeon, Node 24.19.0, pnpm 12.8.1 and Chromium 151.0.7922.34 give non-board JavaScript gzip min/median/max of 386.486/386.486/386.486 KiB on master 35a9d072c and 386.560/386.560/386.560 KiB with send recovery. Validating the call path with Effect Schema instead of zod, which also removes zod and its English locale from the call JavaScript, cut 2.1 KiB (386.5 to 384.5 KiB on the same machine), so the non-board ceiling went down from 387 to 385 KiB. Board, CSS, timing, video-quality and leak limits and the historical timing baseline remain unchanged. The route limit alone falls, from 219 to 217 KiB. The route CSS ceiling is 28 KiB: it rose from 32 to 33 for the transcript language picker (#880) and fell to 28 in #919. Moving the SDK and UI styles onto the design-token scale (#875) turns values such as 12px into var(--space-3) inside the SDK CSS-in-JS strings, which adds 0.4 KiB gzip (385.4 KiB measured by the CI call-performance lane against 385), so the non-board ceiling goes from 385 to 386 KiB. CSS stays at 49.3 of 54 KiB. Setting the entries back to 385 undoes it. The action.* limits moved here unchanged from the latency kit's own budget file. Proposed from 40 kept cycles per plane on staging: one headless and one headed Chromium run from a 4 vCPU droplet in DigitalOcean sgp1 on 7 Nov 2026. Each p95Ms is 1.5 times the larger of the two runs' p95, rounded up to 50 ms. A limit that differs by media plane is keyed by the plane first, for example chalk_sfu.action.leave_ms; the cf_sfu ones gate only the Cloudflare latency run, with interim limits. The SFU loopback and impairment tests are deterministic, so their pass rates must stay at 1 and gate from the start. proof.leave_median_ms gates at the Leave proof's own 5000 ms ceiling on the slowest leave. Every budget gates, and a budget that cannot gate is deleted. A real-node metric gates from the start with a loose ceiling, and a later budgets pull request tightens it once seven nightly values, from at least three nights, show a run-to-run spread below tolerancePct. The 18 chalk_sfu.action.* entries gate from 8 Nov 2026 so the Chalk SFU has a blocking latency budget before nightly values exist: each ceiling is twice the larger p95 of the two 40-cycle runs on 7 Nov 2026 (staging, headless and headed Chromium 151, DigitalOcean sgp1 4 vCPU client, the table in #889), rounded up to 50 ms. They are loose on purpose: the 7-night rule later tightens each one to its real budget in its own pull request. proof.leave_median_ms stays at 5000: the Leave proof takes five samples per run and no run values are kept. On 9 Nov 2026 chalk_sfu.action.camera_toggle.off_ms rose from 650 to 750 and chalk_sfu.action.unpublish.removed_ms from 1000 to 1100. They are interim regression ceilings measured from US-hosted runners (about 200 ms to the Singapore node): p50 636 and 947 against ceilings of 650 and 1000 made the gate depend on the runner's Azure region. They are not the accepted targets, which are much tighter, and the RTT-normalized gate replaces them. On 9 Nov 2026 the web JavaScript gzip ceilings (the 14 web.*.js_gzip_kib entries) rose from 386 to 387 KiB because the receiver's early pull from the Sync media item (#1042) adds 0.16 KiB to a call that was at 386.0; setting them back to 386 undoes it. Later on 10 Nov 2026 the same 14 entries rose from 387 to 388 KiB because the SDK code that lets the Chalk SFU mute a camera or microphone in place (#1043) adds 0.44 KiB to a call that measured 387.4 against a master near 387.0, even while the capability is off; setting them back to 387 undoes it. Later on 10 Nov 2026 the same 14 entries rose from 388 to 389 KiB because the three pull requests that merge together each add code to the call: the Chalk SFU mute in place (#1043, already in master), the receiver socket reuse (#1064) and the gated direct path to Sync (#1066). Five fresh-context bundle-only runs on a 4 vCPU AMD EPYC Linux x64 machine (Instabox), Node 24.21.0, pnpm 12.8.1 and Chromium 151.0.7922.34 give non-board JavaScript gzip min/median/max of 387.175/387.175/387.175 KiB on master 0ea7ed487 and 388.239/388.239/388.239 KiB on a throwaway merge of that master with #1064 (159d09a58) and #1066 (bd54bd99b), so the two add 1.064 KiB. The runs have no spread because the bytes come from one build: the first run builds and the other four reuse it. The ceiling keeps 0.76 KiB of room over the combined size. The board ceilings stay at 743 KiB against 736.667 KiB measured. Setting the 14 entries back to 388 undoes it. Retain the camera capture/picker integration allowance of 1 KiB above the master ceiling of 389 KiB: the 14 non-board JavaScript entries use 390 KiB. Historical five fresh-context bundle-only runs per revision on the same environment gave non-board JavaScript gzip min/median/max of 384.525/384.525/384.525 KiB on master 16ab8a71d and 385.493/385.493/385.493 KiB on camera revision 548fcd65c, a 0.25% integration cost; presets and segmentation remain lazy. Later on 10 Nov 2026 the same 14 entries rose from 390 to 391 KiB because the SDK safety valve that replaces the media connection before its offer reaches the media node's 64 KiB cap (#1098) adds 0.5 KiB to the call. Five fresh-context bundle-only runs on a 4 vCPU Instabox Linux x64 machine give non-board JavaScript gzip of 389.9 KiB on master 039c3b1 and 390.4 KiB on #1098 (b3b6498), the same environment, with no spread because the bytes come from one build; setting the 14 entries back to 390 undoes it. On 10 Nov 2026 the same 14 entries rose from 391 to 392 KiB because the direct signalling door (#1117: the grant door for SFU signalling and Sync, the Tunnel fallback and the path records) adds 0.6 KiB to the call. One build per revision on a 4 vCPU Instabox Linux x64 machine gives non-board JavaScript gzip of 390.9 KiB on master ff8e59a and 391.5 KiB on #1117 (6160197), the same environment, with no spread because the bytes come from one build; no cheap cut exists, since the code is the fallback logic itself and is not lazy-loadable without delaying the first join. Setting the 14 entries back to 391 undoes it. On 10 Nov 2026 the two board JavaScript entries (web.laptop.board.js_gzip_kib and web.phone.board.js_gzip_kib) rose from 743 to 744 KiB because the whiteboard toolbar (#1134) loads the board as its own chunk on first use. That takes the non-board call JavaScript from 391.5 to 374.4 KiB, and the board scenario pays for a second gzip stream plus the toolbar code itself. One build per revision on a 4 vCPU Instabox Linux x64 machine gives board JavaScript gzip of 740.0 KiB on master and 743.5 KiB on #1134, the same environment, with no spread because the bytes come from one build. Trimming the toolbar code and lazy-loading its clear dialog did not bring the board under 743: the dialog chunk split React out of the call bundle and made the board scenario 745.3 KiB. Setting the two entries back to 743 undoes it. Later on 10 Nov 2026 the same 14 entries rose from 392 to 394 KiB because the call dock polish (the tracing loader on the mic and camera icons, the hand-aware reactions button and the per-emoji tray motion) adds SDK styles and glyphs to the call: the CI call-performance lane measured 391.5 KiB for the branch on top of a master that gated at 391, and master has since grown by 0.6 KiB (#1117), so the merged call is expected near 392.5 KiB. A Mac mini bundle-only run (Node 24) gave 390.7 KiB before that merge. Setting the 14 entries back to 392 undoes it. Later on 11 Nov 2026 the two board JavaScript entries rose from 744 to 746 KiB because the call dock polish (#1110) adds 2.0 KiB to the call chunk that the board scenario also loads: the CI call-performance lane measured 745.5 KiB board JavaScript for the branch on top of master with the lazy whiteboard toolbar (#1134), against 743.5 there. Setting the two entries back to 744 undoes it. Later on 11 Nov 2026 the two board JavaScript entries rose from 746 to 751 KiB because the call connection states (#1160: the connection status card, the held last frame behind it and the guest link quality) add to the call chunk that the board scenario also loads: the CI call-performance lane measured 750.1 KiB board JavaScript and 380.9 KiB non-board JavaScript for the branch on top of master with the dock polish (#1110), the call menu (#1111) and the device access card (#1113). The non-board ceiling of 394 KiB holds. Setting the two entries back to 746 undoes it. Later on 11 Nov 2026 the route CSS ceiling rose from 28 to 28.5 KiB and the two board JavaScript entries from 751 to 754 KiB because the phone bottom sheets (#1168) put the shared sheet shell, the drag-to-dismiss logic and hold-to-open on every call: the CI call-performance lane measured 28.1 KiB of route CSS for that branch against 27.9 on master, and 753.7 KiB of board JavaScript against 750.1 (non-board JavaScript 384.5 against 380.9), after the reactions sheet, the device sheet and their CSS were already moved into lazy chunks. The 14 non-board JavaScript entries stay at 394 KiB, which holds against the lazy whiteboard (#1134). Setting the route CSS back to 28 and the board entries back to 751 undoes it. The sfu.loss_pct, sfu.stalls_per_class_hour, sfu.admission_refusals and proof.join_startup.* entries are deleted because nothing produced their metrics. On 13 Nov 2026 the board JavaScript fell from 755.0 to 746.8 KiB while its two ceilings stay at 755 KiB, so call changes that the board scenario also loads have room again: one build per revision on a 4 vCPU Instabox Linux x64 machine gives 755.0 KiB on master dcc9a7260, 753.7 KiB after Excalidraw's @radix-ui/react-tabs 1.0.2 is overridden to 1.1.3 (it then shares the 1.1 primitives that @radix-ui/react-popover already loads instead of bundling a second, older set), and 746.8 KiB after the hosted app resolves Excalidraw's pako import to fflate (apps/web/src/lib/excalidraw-pako.ts), which reads and writes the same zlib stream and, like pako, checks its Adler-32 trailer. The non-board JavaScript stays at 385.6 KiB. All other limits and run settings are unchanged. The route JavaScript limit goes from 217 to 218 KiB for the disconnected screen and the Start call request key (#1320): the CI call-performance lane measured 217.09 KiB against 217 on a base that already sat at the limit. Setting the entry back to 217 undoes it. A gated action metric needs 48 samples out of the full 60-cycle latency run (80%): the percentiles of fewer hide a regression (gatedSamples). Moving the floor from the evaluator into this file puts it under the same rule as every other limit; the value is unchanged. A gated millisecond metric of the Chalk SFU latency verdict also fails when its p95 is more than 50% and more than 200 ms above the median p95 of the last 7 passing records of the same plane and runner, and only warns with fewer than 3 such records (latencyRegression). A replay on the 29 latency records of 26 cuts blocks 2, both already over budget; same-commit runs differ by 6 to 25% on 17 of 18 gated metrics, so a 25% limit would block normal noise. Removed the cf_sfu.action.* budgets because Cloudflare Realtime no longer serves Chalk calls or runs latency proofs. Historical scorecards remain readable; the chalk_sfu.action.* budgets are unchanged. The observability foundation (#1512) adds call JavaScript that the CI call-performance lane measured at 399.4 KiB non-board, 760.7 KiB board and 219.1 KiB route against 394, 755 and 219 on master (one bundle-only run on Linux x64, Chromium 154), so the 14 non-board entries go from 394 to 400, both board entries from 755 to 761 and the route from 219 to 220. CSS, timing, video-quality and leak limits are unchanged. The call-surface and dashboard stack (#1257, #1225, #1287) on top of that measured 400.7 KiB non-board, 402.1 KiB for phone panels, 762.1 KiB board and 220.9 KiB route (one bundle-only run on Linux x64, Chromium 154), so the non-board entries go from 400 to 401, phone panels to 403, both board entries from 761 to 763 and the route from 220 to 221. Setting the entries back undoes it. On 27 Nov 2026 the 14 non-board entries went from 401 to 402, phone panels from 403 to 404 and both board entries from 764 to 765 KiB because the participant device badge (#1628) adds the Chalk tooltip trigger and a small device icon to the participant tile: the Instabox gate measured 401.1 non-board, 402.5 phone panels and 764.3 board against 401, 403 and 764 (one bundle-only run on a 2 vCPU Instabox Linux x64 machine). The route JavaScript entry also went from 221 to 222 KiB: the CI-like Instabox lane measured 221.4 KiB with the badge against 221.3 without it (221.3 against 221 on master already). Setting the entries back undoes it. Presenting a file on the Stage with a header over the page, a page-shaped placeholder and drop feedback (#1766) adds about 2.5 KiB of gzip to the call bundle, so the call JavaScript ceilings rise by 3 KiB (the board by 2.5 KiB) and the route CSS ceiling by 0.5 KiB. Office and OpenDocument files on the Stage (#1774) add the file-type badge, the longer format list and spreadsheet zoom to the call chunk that the board scenario also loads: the CI call-performance lane measured 768.6 KiB board JavaScript against 765 on master, and 405.4 KiB non-board JavaScript against 401 with the 14 non-board ceilings at 406, so only the two board entries go from 768 to 770 KiB. Setting them back to 768 undoes it. The AI participant badge and description line (#1629) add the AI chip, the participant identity kind and the optional description to the participant tile and the people panel: the CI call-performance lane measured 406.0 KiB non-board, 407.4 KiB phone panels and 222.2 KiB route JavaScript against ceilings of 406, 407 and 222 (one bundle-only run on Linux x64), so the 14 non-board entries go up 1 KiB (406 to 407, phone panels 407 to 408) and the route from 222 to 223. Board JavaScript measured 769.3 KiB against 770 and stays. Setting the entries back undoes it. The lobby that names who is already in the call (#1638: the participants line, the sparkle after AI names and the face-hash avatar for the camera-off preview) adds 1.8 KiB to the entrance route: one bundle-only run on Linux x64 measured 223.8 KiB locally and the CI call-performance lane 224.1 KiB, against 222.0 on master. The "N others" list loads on its own, because as part of the route it added 46 KiB (the popover and its positioning code), so only the line and avatars count here. The route JavaScript ceiling goes from 223 to 225. Setting it back to 223 undoes it. With master at a1b0fb9c0 (#1777) the CI call-performance lane measured the merged lobby change (#1638) at 407.8 KiB non-board, 771.0 KiB board and 224.1 KiB route JavaScript, against master at 404.4, 765.7 and 221.9 on a bundle-only run on Linux x64: the line that names who is in the call, the roster read and the face-hash avatars add to the call chunk that every scenario loads. The 14 non-board entries go up 2 KiB (407 to 409, phone panels 408 to 410) and both board entries from 770 to 772. Setting them back undoes it. The platform recovery steps for a refused microphone, camera or screen share (the join-time refusal hook, the dock controls and the refusal latch) add under 1 KiB to the phone panels call: the CI call-performance lane scored it 0.19% above the master baseline of 409 KiB and over the ceiling of 410 (one bundle-only run on Linux x64), so only the phone panels entry goes from 410 to 411. The card and its steps stay in the lazy device access chunk. Setting it back to 410 undoes it. Focus (attention tracking: the tile away chip, the own-status pill, the one-time notice, the allowance rows and the step-away menu) adds about 2.8 KiB of gzip to the call chunk that the board scenario also loads: the CI call-performance lane measured 408.8 KiB non-board JavaScript, 410.2 KiB for phone panels and 772.0 KiB board on a base where the ceilings were 406, 407 and 770 (one bundle-only run on a 2 vCPU Instabox Linux x64 machine), so the non-board ceilings rise by 3 KiB and the board ceilings by 3 KiB over master's. After the lobby that names who is in the call (#1638) landed on master, those ceilings were 409, 410 and 772, so the ceilings are set from a bundle-only run of the merged branch (head a9a32a17e) on a 2 vCPU Instabox Linux x64 machine, rounded up to the next whole KiB: 412.2 KiB non-board JavaScript (ceiling 413), 413.6 KiB for phone panels (414) and 775.4 KiB board (776), measured again after master's #1782 and #1783 merged, with the route at 224.1 KiB JavaScript and 28.7 KiB CSS under their existing ceilings of 225 and 29. Setting them back undoes it.
